title: Six months at a Portsmouth club, then to Washington in 1935
summary: Francis Whitby wrote that he had a club job in Portsmouth; Phillips, Red Elkins and others played it for six months in 1934 and he reached Washington in February 1935.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: You had a job you were heading for? All you guys were heading for a job?
Oh, King's band had a job.

No, no, no. See, Francis Whitby, he stayed in Portsmouth. He was sick. And he wrote a letter and told us that he knew the band wasn't doing nothing, and he had a good job for us. And he kind of wanted to come. He said he'd like to have me and Red and Sam and Charlie and Duff -- that was it. Because we didn't have no bass.
We went to that, and stayed in there for about six months in this club in Portsmouth.
That was in the summer of '34.
And all the way up until the winter.
I left there and came to Washington in 1935.
I think I remember the name of the person you mentioned before who I think you said King Oliver liked a lot. Was it Louis Metcalf?
Clyde Bernhardt, the trombonist, was saying that King Oliver liked Louis Metcalf.
But that's not the one you were thinking of.
